newsitem.title: GERMANY: Postponing EMU not a disaster - German adviser.
newsitem.headline: Postponing EMU not a disaster - German adviser.

text.p: France may call for a delay of European monetary union in view of its difficulties in meeting the Maastricht criteria but a postponement would not be a disaster, a leading German economic adviser was quoted as saying on Monday.

"It would be possible that the initiative may come from France to contemplate a postponement now," Herbert Hax, chairman of the council of advisers to the government known as the "five wise men," told Handelsblatt newspaper in an interview.
Europe's Economic and Monetary Union (EMU) could not start without France, Hax said.

The fact that France was not meeting the criteria "in the way it should and perhaps also could fulfil them" would only cause a dilemma if the January 1, 1999 launch date for EMU was regarded as sacrosanct.
Hax has repeatedly called for a delay to EMU.

French Finance Minister Dominique Strauss-Kahn has already said France will not be able to reduce its budget deficit to 3.0 percent of gross domestic product this year -- the ceiling set by Maastricht for nations seeking to join EMU.
The French government is awaiting an audit of public finances due on July 21 before taking further action.
Hax also said a delay would not cause major currency turbulence and a sharp appreciation of the mark.
"If nations continue their stability efforts in a credible way after a postponement there will be no currency turbulence.
"Whoever claims the contrary is basically saying that all the consolidation efforts should not be taken seriously and that we must introduce the euro by force to cover up a lack of convergence."
